newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-RIVAL COACHES SEARCH FOR MAGIC FORMULA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-RIVAL COACHES SEARCH FOR MAGIC FORMULA.

text.p: Australia and Ireland could make or break the careers of their respective coaches at Lansdowne on Saturday as supporters struggle to keep pace with their sides' latest selection merry-go-round.

The same ground in 1991 witnessed one of rugby's most exciting finales as the Wallabies scored in injury-time to deny the Irish a place in the World Cup semifinals, but Greg Smith and Murray Kidd are currently in no mood for flashbacks.

Smith has made six changes, two of them positional to the team who beat Scotland 29-19 a fortnight ago, while New Zealander Kidd retains just six of the Irish side who lost 40-25 to Western Samoa last week.
In the professional era, both can ill-afford such gambles to misfire, which may explain why the flashest back of all, David Campese, is still missing from the Wallaby test side.
Campese won his 100th cap against Italy but has since become an increasingly frustrated spectator as first Tim Horan and then a second specialist centre Jason Little have been preferred on the wing.

Talented Queensland teenager Ben Tune has also failed to get a look-in, despite the general impression the Wallaby back-line, with the exception of Matthew Burke and David Knox, has lost some of its old swagger.

Former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer has already said he has no idea which direction the team is heading, and Smith's efforts to establish a pattern were scarcely helped when bad weather removed the last midweek fixture before the Irish test.
Even so, Smith would scarcely wish to change places with Kidd whose Irish sides have flattered only to deceive.

They were hit by some spectacular Samoan tries but the depth of talent available is reflected by the statistic that, until scrum-half and captain Niall Hogan withdrew, the only man winning his first full cap was 22-year-old wing Dominic Crotty from Garryowen.

Irish watchers are accustomed to their team confounding all pre-match expectations and, so far, this has been an injury- prone, non-vintage Wallaby side. Even so, Kidd's prayers seem unlikely to be answered.

Ireland - 15-Jim Staples; 14-James Topping, 13-Jonathan Bell, 12-Mark McCall, 11-Dominic Crotty; 10-Paul Burke, 9-Steve McIvor; 8-Anthony Foley, 7-Denis McBride, 6-David Corkery, 5- Jeremy Davidson, 4-Gabriel Fulcher, 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Keith Wood (captain), 1-Nick Popplewell.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Jason Little, 13-Daniel Herbert, 12-Tim Horan, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Michael Brial, 7-David Wilson, 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Warwick Waugh, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Dan Crowley.
